target_customer: Filipino aspiring software engineers who pay tuition after getting hired, and the remote employers who hire them
problem: Filipinos lack affordable, job-linked training to become remote software engineers for global companies.
business_model: Bootcamp tuition deferred until hire via an income share style agreement (17 percent of salary for 2 years per the school site), plus installment plans

founders.name: Victor Rivera
founders.background_notes: Per e27 July 2020. Education not stated in sources opened.

founders.name: John Young
founders.background_notes: Per e27 July 2020 (various product roles). YC page lists him as a former founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Curriculum, learning platform and hiring pipeline are standard edtech work; the difficulty was operations and job placement, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Employer partnerships such as Xendit and PayMongo helped, but bootcamps with deferred payment were copyable and the school does not hold unique technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent buying or copying Avion.

market_need_then: Remote work demand rose in 2020 and the Philippines has a large outsourcing workforce; coverage in January 2021 described a college dropout founder training Filipinos for remote engineering jobs. Seven batches had graduated by February 2021 per KrASIA.

branding.domain_note: avionschool.com, a name plus descriptor domain

identity.voice_and_tone: Career and outcome focused, with graduate testimonials

branding.brand_signature: Pay after you are hired promise
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Rappler, Manila Bulletin, e27 and NoypiGeeks; no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Solid local press but no evidence of a distinctive brand driver; the name echoes aviation and searches return aviation schools.

outcome_analysis: Avion School raised a pre-seed from angel investors in 2020 and a $125,000 YC investment in early 2021 while growing graduate batches. The YC directory marks it inactive and lists John Young as a former founder, but the school website still appeared live with a 2024 footer, so the inactive label may reflect only the YC record. No shutdown cause is public, and no later round was found.
notes: Two outlets (e27, KrASIA) cover the rounds. The e27 page shows no publication date; July 2020 is inferred from its URL. A mid-2020 name for the YC deal is shown by KrASIA as 9 February 2021. Rappler and Manila Bulletin pages were not opened (403 or snippet only). Status conflict: YC lists Inactive while the site appears live. Competitor list empty: Zuitt appears only in undated pages, so it is not listed as a dated competitor.
